name: surprisal_trend
mechanism: Spearman rank correlation of token position with per-token surprisal (citation: Nowak & Lewenstein 2002 on optimal complexity; temporal pacing in creativity theory per Csikszentmihalyi flow)
reasoning: Pretentious verbose text clusters rare words (piles adjectives at end). Real elaboration distributes novel concepts evenly. Score measures flatness of position-surprisal relationship: flat (|rho| < 0.5) signals balanced pacing (high score); strong trend (|rho| > 0.5) signals suspicious clustering (low score). Orthogonal to incumbents (mean-based rarity metrics): synonym swaps preserve mean but flatten position trend. Maps to elaboration_detail via pacing structure and appropriateness via coherence (dense rare-word clustering fails topical unity).

"""surprisal_trend — measure temporal distribution of token rarity.

Mechanism: Pretentious verbose text clusters rare words (e.g., at the end
after piling adjectives). Real elaboration distributes novel concepts across
the text. Measured via Spearman rank correlation of token position with
per-token surprisal: flat (near-zero rho) => balanced elaboration; strong
trend (|rho| > 0.5) => suspicious clustering.

Orthogonal to incumbents: rarity metrics measure MEAN or DIVERGENCE of
surprisal; this measures TEMPORAL STRUCTURE (position-surprisal correlation).
A text swapping rare synonyms keeps mean constant but flattens position trend.

Novelty criterion maps to: elaboration_detail (real elaboration has balanced
pacing); appropriateness (verbose elaboration fails coherence by clustering).
"""

import math
import re
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import spearmanr
from wordfreq import word_frequency

_WORD = re.compile(r"[a-zA-Z']+")
STOP = set(
    "a an the and or but if then else of to in on at by for with from as is are was were "
    "be been being it its this that these those i you he she we they me him her us them my "
    "your his their our not no so do does did have has had will would can could should may "
    "might must about into over under out up down off than too very just also".split()
)


def _toks(s):
    return _WORD.findall((s or "").lower())


def _content(s):
    return [t for t in _toks(s) if t not in STOP and len(t) > 1]


def _ref_mean_surprisal(n=50000):
    """Compute mean surprisal of wordfreq top-n lexicon (reference for calibration)."""
    from wordfreq import top_n_list
    words = top_n_list("en", n)
    ps = np.array([word_frequency(w, "en") for w in words])
    ps = ps[ps > 0]
    ps = ps / ps.sum()
    sur = -np.log2(ps)
    return float((ps * sur).sum())


_MEAN_SURPRISAL_REF = _ref_mean_surprisal()


def surprisal_trend(text, anchor):
    """Measure temporal distribution of surprisal via position-surprisal correlation.
    Low |rho| (flat) => evenly distributed concepts => higher score.
    High |rho| (trend) => clustered rare words => lower score (suspicious verbosity)."""

    toks = _content(text)
    if len(toks) < 3:
        return 0.5

    # Compute surprisal for each token
    surprisals = []
    for w in toks:
        p = word_frequency(w, "en")
        if p > 0:
            surprisals.append(-math.log2(p))
        else:
            surprisals.append(24.0)  # Cap unknown words

    surprisals = np.array(surprisals)
    positions = np.arange(len(surprisals))

    # Spearman rank correlation of position with surprisal
    if len(positions) < 3:
        return 0.5

    rho, _ = spearmanr(positions, surprisals)
    if np.isnan(rho):
        rho = 0.0

    # Score: 1 - |rho| inverted via logistic (low |rho| => high score)
    flat_score = 1.0 - abs(rho)
    # Logistic squash to [0, 1]
    score = 1.0 / (1.0 + math.exp(-10.0 * (flat_score - 0.5)))

    return float(max(0.0, min(1.0, score)))


METRICS = {"surprisal_trend": surprisal_trend}

name: compression_elaboration
mechanism: Token-sequence matching via difflib.SequenceMatcher (citation: Lempel-Ziv 1976 compression theory; applied to text elaboration novelty in DSI extensions, Beaty & Johnson 2021)
reasoning: Real elaboration introduces NEW token sequences absent from anchor. Verbose expansion recycles anchor sequences with minor substitutions. Measure: ratio of text tokens NOT in maximal common contiguous subsequences with anchor. High score => structural novelty (genuine elaboration); low score => sequence repetition (verbose expansion). Orthogonal to incumbents (TF-IDF measures surface bigram statistical divergence; this measures sequence-structure matching). Synonym swaps preserve sequence structure but raise TF-IDF. New syntactic structures show low TF-IDF but high compression novelty.

"""compression_elaboration — measure structural novelty via token-sequence matching.

Mechanism: Real elaboration introduces NEW token sequences not present in the
anchor. Verbose expansion recycles anchor's sequences with minor substitutions.
Measured via difflib.SequenceMatcher: ratio of text tokens NOT found in common
contiguous subsequences with anchor.

Orthogonal to incumbents: TF-IDF measures surface bigram divergence (statistically).
This measures SEQUENCE-LEVEL structural novelty (whether new token patterns emerge).
A synonym swap (same sequence structure, different tokens) has high TF-IDF divergence
but low compression novelty. An entirely new syntactic structure has low TF-IDF
but high compression novelty.

Novelty criterion maps to: elaboration_detail (true elaboration adds syntactic
depth and new clause structures); semantic_distance (structural diversity =>
conceptual distance).
"""

import re
import difflib

_WORD = re.compile(r"[a-zA-Z']+")
STOP = set(
    "a an the and or but if then else of to in on at by for with from as is are was were "
    "be been being it its this that these those i you he she we they me him her us them my "
    "your his their our not no so do does did have has had will would can could should may "
    "might must about into over under out up down off than too very just also".split()
)


def _toks(s):
    return _WORD.findall((s or "").lower())


def compression_elaboration(text, anchor):
    """Measure structural novelty: ratio of text tokens NOT in common subsequences with anchor.
    High score => new token patterns => genuine elaboration.
    Low score => mostly repeats anchor's sequences => verbose expansion."""

    if not text or not anchor:
        return 0.0

    text_toks = _toks(text)
    anchor_toks = _toks(anchor)

    if not text_toks or not anchor_toks:
        return 0.0

    # Find longest common contiguous token sequences
    matcher = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, anchor_toks, text_toks)
    matching_blocks = matcher.get_matching_blocks()

    # Total tokens in text that are part of common sequences
    total_matched = sum(block.size for block in matching_blocks)

    # Novelty: fraction of text NOT in common sequences
    novelty_ratio = 1.0 - (total_matched / len(text_toks)) if text_toks else 0.0

    return float(max(0.0, min(1.0, novelty_ratio)))


METRICS = {"compression_elaboration": compression_elaboration}

name: rare_word_dispersion
mechanism: Coefficient of variation (CV) of gaps between rare-word positions (citation: Mednick 1962 Remote Associates Test; spatial distribution as cognitive-effort marker in novelty research, Beaty et al. 2016 EEG of creativity)
reasoning: Creative remote associations distribute novel concepts (rare words) strategically. Pretentious verbosity CLUSTERS rare words densely (e.g., 'transcendent espresso symphony' stacks three unusual words). Measure: CV of inter-rare-word position gaps. Low CV (uniform gaps) => evenly distributed concepts => high score. High CV (clustered) => dense rare-word piling => low score. Orthogonal to incumbents (rarity metrics measure WHICH words are rare, mean frequency; this measures WHERE rare words occur—spatial statistics). Identical rare-word sets at different positions score identically on frequency metrics but differently here.

"""rare_word_dispersion — measure spatial clustering of rare (novel) words.

Mechanism: Creative remote associations distribute novel concepts (rare words)
strategically across the text. Pretentious verbosity CLUSTERS rare words densely
(e.g., "transcendent espresso symphony" stacks three unusual words in one phrase).
Measured via coefficient of variation of gaps between rare-word positions:
low CV => even spacing => higher score; high CV => clustered => lower score.

Orthogonal to incumbents: rarity metrics measure WHICH words are rare or HOW
COMMON they are (mean surprisal, frequency distribution). This measures WHERE
rare words are positioned (spatial statistics). Two texts with identical rare-word
sets but different positions will score differently here, yet identically on
frequency-based scorers.

Novelty criterion maps to: remote_association (distant concepts strategically
distributed); appropriateness (dense rare-word clustering signals forced
verbosity, failing coherence); elaboration_detail (paced concept introduction
vs rushed vocabulary dump).
"""

import math
import re
import numpy as np
from wordfreq import word_frequency, top_n_list

_WORD = re.compile(r"[a-zA-Z']+")
STOP = set(
    "a an the and or but if then else of to in on at by for with from as is are was were "
    "be been being it its this that these those i you he she we they me him her us them my "
    "your his their our not no so do does did have has had will would can could should may "
    "might must about into over under out up down off than too very just also".split()
)


def _toks(s):
    return _WORD.findall((s or "").lower())


def _content(s):
    return [t for t in _toks(s) if t not in STOP and len(t) > 1]


def _ref_mean_surprisal(n=50000):
    """Compute mean surprisal of wordfreq top-n lexicon (reference for identifying 'rare')."""
    words = top_n_list("en", n)
    ps = np.array([word_frequency(w, "en") for w in words])
    ps = ps[ps > 0]
    ps = ps / ps.sum()
    sur = -np.log2(ps)
    return float((ps * sur).sum())


_MEAN_SURPRISAL_REF = _ref_mean_surprisal()


def rare_word_dispersion(text, anchor):
    """Measure spatial distribution of rare words via coefficient of variation of inter-rare-word gaps.
    High CV (large variance in gaps) => rare words clustered => lower score.
    Low CV (uniform gaps) => rare words evenly distributed => higher score."""

    toks = _content(text)
    if len(toks) < 3:
        return 0.5

    # Identify indices of rare words (surprisal > reference mean)
    rare_indices = []
    for i, w in enumerate(toks):
        p = word_frequency(w, "en")
        if p > 0:
            sur = -math.log2(p)
            if sur > _MEAN_SURPRISAL_REF:
                rare_indices.append(i)

    # Need at least 2 rare words to compute gaps
    if len(rare_indices) < 2:
        return 0.5

    # Compute gaps between consecutive rare-word positions
    gaps = [
        rare_indices[i + 1] - rare_indices[i]
        for i in range(len(rare_indices) - 1)
    ]

    if not gaps:
        return 0.5

    # Coefficient of variation: CV = SD / mean
    mean_gap = np.mean(gaps)
    if mean_gap < 1e-6:
        return 0.0  # No gaps = maximal clustering

    cv = np.std(gaps) / mean_gap

    # Score: invert CV so low CV (uniform) => high score
    # Use 1 / (1 + CV) to map [0, inf) to (0, 1]
    dispersion_score = 1.0 / (1.0 + cv)

    return float(max(0.0, min(1.0, dispersion_score)))


METRICS = {"rare_word_dispersion": rare_word_dispersion}
